summary: This regulation requires listed companies to create and review a policy on dealing with related party transactions. It sets rules for getting approvals from the audit committee and the shareholders before entering into such deals. Certain transactions also have rules for later approval, known as ratification.
points: The listed entity must create a policy on material related party transactions approved by its board of directors.
The board of directors must review the policy at least once every three years.
All related party transactions and subsequent material modifications need prior approval from independent directors on the audit committee.
Material related party transactions and material modifications need prior approval from shareholders through a resolution.
No related party is allowed to vote to approve such shareholder resolutions.
example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is a listed company. It wants to buy raw materials from a company owned by the brother of one of its directors. Because this is a related party, Meera Textiles must follow strict rules. First, the deal requires prior approval from the audit committee, and only the members who are independent directors can approve it. If the deal is considered material under the company policy, the shareholders must also approve it in a meeting. No related party is allowed to vote on this shareholder approval.

terms.meaning: A person or company connected to the listed entity, such as through ownership or family ties.
A committee of directors that oversees financial reporting and specific company transactions.
A board member who does not have any material or pecuniary relationship with the company.
The act of giving formal approval to an action after it has already taken place.

watch: People often confuse prior approval requirements with later ratification, but ratification is only allowed under specific strict conditions.
